Title: How to Fix Sour or Acidic Tomato Sauce
Description: Tomato sauce tastes sharp or sour? Some canned tomatoes are more acidic than others. Let the sauce simmer a little longer, then add a small pinch of sugar or a knob of butter and taste again. A grated carrot cooked in at the start helps too. Go slowly: you want it rounded, not sweet. Title: How Much Salt in Pasta Water? The Restaurant Rule
Description: Restaurant pasta tastes seasoned all the way through because the cooks salt the water. Bring a big pot to a rolling boil, add salt until the water tastes pleasantly salty, then add the pasta and stir. The pasta absorbs that seasoning as it cooks, so you need less salt in the sauce. Title: Bronze-Cut Pasta — How to Spot Better Pasta at the Store
Description: Better pasta isn't about the fanciest brand. Look for "bronze-cut" or "bronze die" on the bag: it means the pasta was pushed through bronze dies, which leaves a rough, dull surface that holds on to sauce. Title: Dry Brine Your Turkey — Salt It a Day Ahead for Better Flavor
Description: The easy restaurant-style trick for a better holiday turkey: a dry brine. Season the bird all over with salt (and pepper or herbs if you like) a day or two ahead and leave it in the fridge, uncovered, on a tray. The salt seasons the meat and the skin dries out so it roasts crisper. Follow the safe thawing and cooking times on the label. Holiday tips on Sal's page.

Title: Steakhouse-Style Mashed Potatoes — Warm the Milk and Butter
Description: For creamy, steakhouse-style mashed potatoes, warm the milk and butter before they go in. Cold dairy cools the potatoes so you end up working them more, and overworked potatoes go gluey. Drain the potatoes well, let them steam dry for a minute, mash gently and season at the end. Never use a blender. Holiday side dish tips on Sal's page.

Title: Restaurant Pan Sauce Secret — Finish With Cold Butter
Description: Restaurant pan sauces look glossy and taste rich because of one last step: off the heat, swirl in a small piece of cold butter until it melts into the sauce. Title: How to Reheat Leftover Pasta So It Tastes Fresh
Description: Leftover pasta dries out because the pasta keeps soaking up sauce in the fridge. Put it in a pan with a splash of water, broth or extra sauce, cover it and warm it over low heat, stirring now and then until hot all the way through.
